fields.title: EQ
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › EQ — The EQ unit provides 3-bands of fully parametric equalizing. This high-quality algorithm has a much better response at high frequencies than digital equalizers usually have. Heard in patches: Basses, Pads, Leads, Keys, Plucks, Drums; e.g. Xpander 1, Smooth Stabs, MG, Hugeness, Embarrass.

fields.title: Exciter
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Exciter — Exciter is a harmonic exciter based on the famous Aphex Aural Exciter unit. For more information, see this blog post by Jatin Chowdhury. Heard in patches: Keys, Sequences, Percussion, Basses; e.g. Sluggish, Membranophone Dum-Tek, Amethyst Empathy, FM Square Glassy Boops, Distorted Power Bass Guitar.

fields.title: Graphic EQ
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Graphic EQ — Graphic EQ is, as its name suggests, a graphic equalizer. It is comprised of 11 level-adjustable and deactivatable (from the right-click menu) bands, which makes this equalizer better than the normal EQ at sculpting relatively complex response curves. Apart from the fact that there is also an output gain control at the bottom of the interface, there is not much else to add. Heard in patches: Pads, Drums, Keys, Basses, FX, Winds; e.g. Kick 2, Kick 4, Tuned Wood, Ritual, Slow Mono.

fields.title: Resonator
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Resonator — The Resonator provides carefully tuned lowpass, bandpass, bandpass + notch or highpass filters, each with individual output gain and resonance. By default, the filters cannot be driven into self-oscillation, but if you right-click any of the three Resonance parameters and enable Modulation extends into self-oscillation, modulation sources can drive the filters to a self- oscillating point. Similarly, the three resonator bands are tuned to match the ranges of a very famous resonator circuit, but they can be extended to allow a wider range. Heard in patches: Basses, Percussion, Strings, Winds, Keys, Pads; e.g. VHS, Dead MT, Pocket Bass, So Wavey, The Housewives of Lofi.

fields.title: Bonsai
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Bonsai — Bonsai is an organic-sounding distortion effect, combining a highly non-linear bass boost with an emphasis-filtered waveshaper and noise AM. It excels at a wide range of very beefy gnarly sounds, but can sound very good at subtle settings too. Heard in patches: Basses, Percussion, Bass, Leads; e.g. Nice Kicks, Big Fat Combinator Bass, Brush Your Shoulders Off, Sub Wrap Example, Seek And Ye Shall Find.

fields.title: CHOW
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › CHOW — Chow is a half-wave rectifier distortion effect with controls similar to those found in a compressor. The original effect was implemented as an open source audio plugin by Jatin Chowdhury. Heard in patches: Basses; e.g. Badass, Mod Bass.

fields.title: Distortion
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Distortion — Distortion algorithm. Provides plenty of EQ options as well as a feedback loop to alter the tonality of the clipping stage. Distortion algorithm block diagram Heard in patches: Basses, Drums, Leads, FX, Keys, Sequences; e.g. Lead With A Bell Attack, Pad Plink 'n' Move, Uni 2, Serious Distortion, Rusty.

fields.title: Neuron
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Neuron — Neuron is an effect based on a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), a commonly used building block in recurrent neural networks. For more information on the development of the Neuron effect, you can read this blog post by Jatin Chowdhury. Heard in patches: Basses, Drums, Guitars, Bass, Soundscapes, Sequences; e.g. Legato Bass, Short Snare, Miles Of AM Radio, This Resonates With Me Deeply, Glissabout.

fields.title: Tape
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Tape — Tape effect is a port of the Chow Tape Model tape emulation effect, a real-time physical model of a reel-to-reel analog tape machine. The model contains parameters for controlling the amount of tape distortion and degradation, as well as physical characteristics of the tape machine, like the play head width, or tape thickness. The original plugin can be found on GitHub, and signal processing details are outlined in this 2019 DAFx paper. Heard in patches: Keys, Pads, Soundscapes, Sequences, Basses, Leads; e.g. Journey, Keep Waiting, Slow Mono, Soft Tine Piano, Hollow Code.

fields.title: Waveshaper
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Waveshaper — The full waveshaper module present in the sound shaping section of the synth (see Waveshaper) is also available as an effect unit which, like other effects, can be loaded anywhere in the FX signal path. It also hosts additional controls for further adjustments of the resulting distorted output. Heard in patches: Basses, Keys, Drums, Brass, Percussion, Pads; e.g. Kick 2, Kick 4, Kick 1, Kick Lo-Fi, Ayay.

fields.title: Combulator
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Combulator — Combulator effect is somewhat similar to the Resonator in that it is also made of three filter bands. However, it uses comb filters instead. These three filters are tuned to a center pitch and two offsets, each with its own gain control, and combs 2 and 3 with individual pan. A common use case is to use a monophonic (scene-level) modulation source like Highest Key to modulate the center pitch. The circuit also implements an envelope follower on the input signal, and mixes additional noise in based on the followed envelope and the Extra Noise parameter. Heard in patches: Drums, Strings, Winds, FX, Percussion, Pads; e.g. 10 Example - Both Time And Space, Paraphrase, Organish, Dark Crystal Flute, Vintage Demonic Brass Ensemble.

fields.title: Frequency Shifter
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Frequency Shifter — Based on the classic Bode frequency shifter effect, which uses a carrier wave to shift frequencies linearly. This changes the frequency relationships between overtones, usually resulting in a more inharmonic sound. This version also provides a delay unit and a feedback loop to create consecutively shifted repeating delays, as heard in a classic english sci-fi theme. Heard in patches: Pads, FX, Basses, Leads, Plucks, Sequences; e.g. Retrofit, Blekinge, Endgame, Geiger, Spooky Fish.

fields.title: Nimbus
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Nimbus — The Nimbus effect imports the granular texture effect from Émilie Gillet’s Eurorack project. You can read the manual for the hardware device on which this effect is based here. The labels and ranges in the effect adjust based on the mode to allow you to use this effect appropriately in Surge XT. Heard in patches: FX, Pads, Drums, Sequences, Leads, Keys; e.g. Dark Pulse, Mana Quest, Water, Organish, Slewing Glass.

fields.title: Ring Modulator
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Ring Modulator — Flexible ring modulation algorithm. 1 For more information on the diode model used by the ring modulator, you can read this paper. Heard in patches: Drums, Basses, FX, Plucks, Leads, Percussion; e.g. Wadded Beef, Chaos Bits, Ghoul In The Machine, FM Dubstep Bass, Uncertain Disclosure.

fields.title: Treemonster
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Treemonster — Treemonster is a specialized effect ported from Shortcircuit 2, a proper Vember Audio classic! Treemonster runs a naïve pitch detection algorithm on the input signal, runs a sine oscillator at the detected pitch, then ring modulates the input signal with the resulting tuned sine oscillator. It can get pretty crazy, especially if you apply pitch shifts to the generated oscillator. Like the emulated analog ring modulation in Surge XT, this effect can very rapidly become very inharmonic. Heard in patches: Drums, FX, Basses, Soundscapes; e.g. Tears Of..., Modularesque, Pocket Bass, Broken Furbi, Cheap Hat.

fields.title: Vocoder
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Vocoder — The audio input of Surge XT is used to modulate the carrier signal at the input stage of this 20- band vocoder algorithm. Heard in patches: Vocoder; e.g. Noise, Pop, Solo.

fields.title: Chorus
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Chorus — 4-stage chorus algorithm. Heard in patches: Pads, Keys, Leads, Basses, Rhythms, Plucks; e.g. Licht, Melon, Split Personality, Synth Brass 2, FM Combo.

fields.title: Ensemble
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Ensemble — Ensemble chorus effect based on BBD (bucket-brigade device) delay lines (with optional clean digital delay lines, too). Implementation of the BBD chip is based on a 2018 DAFx paper by Martin Holters and Julian Parker. Heard in patches: Pads, Soundscapes, FX, Sequences, Leads, Atmospheres; e.g. VHS, Ritual, Sluggish, Saturn Saw, Starfall.

fields.title: Flanger
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Flanger — Versatile Flanging algorithm. Heard in patches: Keys, Pads, Ambiance, Leads, Plucks, Soundscapes; e.g. 10 Example - Both Time And Space, 09 Example - Crossfading Oscillators, 05 The Envelope And Its Parameters, 13 Duophony, Neuro.

fields.title: Phaser
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Phaser — Flexible phaser with adjustable number of stages. 1 Once disabled, the Rate parameter acts like a phase parameter, which can be scrubbed through and modulated to achieve manual phasing and combing effects. Heard in patches: Leads, Pads, Basses, Plucks, FX, Keys; e.g. The Elephant Told You, Sticky, MacLaurin, Metal Chonk, Phasey.

fields.title: Rotary Speaker
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Rotary Speaker — Rotary speaker simulator algorithm. Heard in patches: Keys, Organs, FX, Pads, Leads, Basses; e.g. Gentle, Thynchronization, Artificial 1, EP 2, Artificial 2.

fields.title: Delay
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Delay — The delay algorithm in Surge XT is very versatile and can work well both as an echo/delay and chorus. Delay algorithm block diagram There is an LFO connected to the delay-lines (not shown in diagram) which can provide stereo- widening/detuning of the delay-line. Heard in patches: Leads, Pads, Plucks, Keys, Basses, FX; e.g. Moving Day In The Caves, Lead With A Bell Attack, Pad Plink 'n' Move, The Elephant Told You, Bloom.

fields.title: Reverb 1
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Reverb 1 — The Reverb 1 algorithm is a classic and older sounding digital reverb. Heard in patches: Pads, Leads, Keys, FX, Basses, Plucks; e.g. Moving Day In The Caves, Baritonosaurus Saxus, The Elephant Told You, Bloom, Sticky.

fields.title: Reverb 2
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Reverb 2 — The Reverb 2 algorithm is a second version of Surge’s original Reverb effect and has a different algorithm and controls. Reverb 2 is more natural and contains less digital artifacts. For most use cases, Reverb 2 sounds better than Reverb 1. Heard in patches: Pads, Keys, Leads, Plucks, Ambiance, Atmospheres; e.g. 13 Duophony, Snare 2, Kick 1, Clave, Ayay.

fields.title: Spring Reverb
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Spring Reverb — The Spring Reverb algorithm is an emulation of old spring reverb effects. It is based loosely on the algorithm outlined by Parker (EURASIP 2011). Heard in patches: Keys, Basses, Formula Modulator, Atmospheres, Brass, Percussion; e.g. 11 Example - Reich - Piano Phase, Rampage, Boog, Digivex, Alias Digital Atmosphere.

fields.title: Airwindows
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Airwindows — Airwindows effect is an integration of 56 diverse effects by Chris Johnson. Thanks to Airwindows for providing high quality open source effects! You can read more about these effects here, and read the code here. Heard in patches: Pads, Basses, Drums, Keys, FX, Percussion; e.g. 10 Example - Both Time And Space, 09 Example - Crossfading Oscillators, 03 The Init Function And State, Kick 2, Snare 2.

fields.title: Conditioner
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Conditioner — The Conditioner is a simple EQ, stereo image control and a limiter built into one unit. The limiter applies make-up gain automatically. Heard in patches: Basses, Leads, Keys, Plucks, FX, Percussion; e.g. Baritonosaurus Saxus, The Shoebox, Havoc, Uni 1, Flute 1.

fields.title: Audio Input
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Audio Input — The Audio Input provides the same functionality as the Audio In oscillator algorithm, but allows you to insert audio into the effects stage, with is downstream from other voice processing components such as the filters and the waveshaper. Heard in patches: Plucks, Keys, Leads; e.g. July, Cute 1, Cute 2, Cute 3, Let Life Give Limes.

fields.title: Mid-Side Tool
fields.text: Technical Reference › Effects › Mid-Side Tool — The Mid-Side tool is a set of controls useful for transforming a stereo signal to mid-side and vice versa, with additional separate filtering for the mid and side signal. Heard in patches: Basses, Synths, Pads, Drums, FX; e.g. Kick 1, Ayay, Hate, Mammoth, Burial.
